critique.summary: The citywide channels are carrying every plan: the Joel Osteen and Kirk Franklin podcast reads and the Target drop each earn 13–18% of adoption, and A1 doubles the benchmark at $917 per point of reach versus $1824 with the best 10th percentile (7.6%). Local ground spend (social, street teams, single cafés at 0.4–1.7% each) adds little anywhere, and A3's Fort McPherson-heavy ground game trails at $1160 per point and a 4.9% floor.

findings.finding: Reach 8.7% (P10 7.6%, P90 10.2%) at $917 per point; the two podcasts take 29.0% of adoption for $6450, while social:0 ($900, 0.8%) and 404 Coffee (0.4%) are near-dead weight.
Cheapest per point at $896 with 8.4% reach and the strongest Country/Decatur district (10.4%), but its 10th percentile drops to 6.8%, and social:3 ($900) and street:3 ($450) earn only 0.4% each.
Only 6.1% reach (P10 4.9%) at $1160 per point; the Target drop earns 18.2%, but $1800 of social:0 earns 2.3% and the day-31/32 street teams are among the weakest at 0.6%.
4.3% reach at $1824 per point, so all three plans beat it, though A3's 10th percentile of 4.9% barely clears the benchmark's 90th percentile of 5.3%.

changes.change: Build on A1: keep podcast:1F6EECD3 (Joel Osteen) on day 5 and podcast:A9103374 (Kirk Franklin), but move Kirk Franklin from day 12 to around day 3–5, and add collab:BFC8D7B1 (Target drop) from day 0 for 34 days.
changes.why: The two podcasts and the Target drop are the only actions earning double-digit shares of adoption, and running all three early gives word of mouth (around 50% of adoption) the most time to spread.

changes.change: Pay for the Target drop by cutting social:0 ($900) and partner 5D7323AF (404 Coffee, $300) from A1.
changes.why: Together they earned 1.2% of adoption for $1200, while the Target drop earned 13–18% for $2000.

changes.change: Drop the late street teams (street:0 day 31, street:2 day 32) and street:3 in any plan.
changes.why: Each earned 0.4–0.6% of adoption, and launches only 3–4 days out leave no time for word of mouth.

changes.change: Keep only the best ground partners as cheap supplements: House of Fresh (D76FB0CA, 0.8–1.2%) and Community Grounds Cafe (1.7% in A3).
changes.why: They are the strongest $300 local items, and keeping them maintains some presence in zone 0 (fit 0.50) without spending on weak ground actions.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B1

plan.headline: Two faith podcast reads a month out reach 10.3% of the natural audience, 2.4× benchmark
plan.summary: The bet is to run host-read ads on the Joel Osteen Podcast and Good Words with Kirk Franklin early, 31 and 30 days before launch, so word of mouth has a month to spread, backed by a short citywide social burst and two cheap Fort McPherson partners. Qloo taste data shows this audience over-indexes heavily on both shows (affinity 0.93 and 0.92), drawn in by Steve Harvey and Tyler Perry fans, and House of Fresh (0.92) and Community Grounds Cafe (0.84) match the same crowd. In a simulation built on that data, the plan reaches about 10.3% of the natural audience (range 8.6%–11.6%) at $774 per point of reach, against 4.3% and $1,824 for the benchmark, with word of mouth driving 56% of adoption; this is a projection, not a guarantee.

items: 35 days before launch: confirm ad slots and scripts with both podcasts; sign up House of Fresh and Community Grounds Cafe and deliver posters and flyers.
34 days before launch: start targeted social ads across Atlanta, weighted by taste fit, running for 5 days.
31 days before launch: Host-read ad runs on the Joel Osteen Podcast.
30 days before launch: Host-read ad runs on Good Words with Kirk Franklin; the social burst ends 30 days before launch.

weeks.label: 4–1 weeks before launch

Weekly from 28 days before launch: track ticket-link clicks, promo codes, and how buyers say they heard about the show; no new spend is planned.
